clinician.final_diagnosis: Miller-Fisher Syndrome subtype presenting with isolated bilateral mydriasis
clinician.trajectory_summary: 7-year-old girl presented with isolated bilateral painless mydriasis and absent light reflexes for 7 days, no other neurological deficits. Initial imaging and neurological exam were normal. Serum antiganglioside antibodies (anti-GQ1b IgM/IgG and anti-GT1a IgG) were positive confirming immune neuropathy. CSF analysis was negative for albuminocytologic dissociation. Nerve conduction studies and EEG were normal. Detailed neurological exam showed intact cranial nerves, normal motor and sensory function. Treatment with IVIG was administered with normalization of pupils and reflexes within 5 days, sustained at 6 months without progression to classic MFS features.
